summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of sclerosing mesenteritis, recurrent small bowel obstructions, and chronic TPN via a femoral catheter was admitted for worsening abdominal pain and persistent vomiting. Imaging showed no complete bowel obstruction, and the surgical team recommended medical management. She was initially NPO and treated with IV Dilaudid and Phenergan for pain and nausea. Her G tube was replaced as scheduled, and her morphine dose was increased to 25 mg PR every 6 hours due to inadequate pain control. A mechanical complication of her femoral central venous line—repeated splitting of the external portion—led to its replacement. She was transitioned back to home medications, including rectal morphine and Phenergan, with improved symptom control. Social work supported her emotional distress, which was multifactorial. She was discharged home with updated pain management, follow-up plans with gastroenterology, pain clinic, and mental health providers, and no pending studies.
